The one validator of the shared contracts. It supports exactly the keywords in ``SUPPORTED_KEYWORDS`` and the
annotations in ``ANNOTATIONS`` (accepted, never evaluated); any other keyword in a schema file fails closed
with ``SchemaProfileError`` at load time. Validation collects every issue instead of stopping at the first
one. ``load_contract`` loads one contract directory ``<contract>/v<N>/`` of the foundation schemas.

from __future__ import annotations

10→import json
import math
from pathlib import Path
import re
from typing import Any, Iterator, NamedTuple

DIALECT = "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"
CONTRACT_URN_PREFIX = "urn:swissknifeman:aicore:"
ERROR_CODES = ("type", "enum", "const", "required", "additional", "pattern", "min_items", "unique",
               "min_length", "one_of", "ref", "minimum", "maximum", "property_name")
20→SUPPORTED_KEYWORDS = frozenset({
    "$schema", "$id", "$defs", "$ref", "title", "description", "type", "enum", "const", "properties",
    "required", "additionalProperties", "items", "minItems", "uniqueItems", "minLength", "pattern", "oneOf",
    "default", "minimum", "maximum", "patternProperties", "propertyNames",
})
# Keywords a ``propertyNames`` schema may use: a name is a string, so only string checks apply.
_PROPERTY_NAME_KEYWORDS = frozenset({"type", "pattern", "minLength", "description", "enum"})
# Annotations of module configuration schemas: the validator accepts them and ignores them. Any other
# ``x-*`` keyword is outside the profile.

30→_VERSION_DIR = re.compile(r"v[1-9][0-9]*")
_TYPE_NAMES = frozenset({"null", "boolean", "integer", "number", "string", "array", "object"})
_cache: dict[tuple[Path, str, tuple[str, ...], str, tuple[Path, ...]], "Registry"] = {}
_CONTRACT_REF = re.compile(r"([a-z][a-z0-9-]*):(v[1-9][0-9]*)")
_SET_ID = re.compile(r"(.+:)([a-z][a-z0-9-]*):(v[1-9][0-9]*)")
_FOUNDATION_SCHEMAS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "schemas"


class SchemaProfileError(ValueError):
    """A schema file leaves the closed profile, or an unknown schema kind was requested."""
40→

class RefError(LookupError):

    path: str  # JSON pointer such as "/reads/2/path"; "" is the document root
    code: str
    message: str

class Registry:
    """Loaded schemas by ``$id``; read-only after construction."""

    def __init__(self, schemas: dict[str, dict], *, urn_prefix: str, kinds: tuple[str, ...], version: str = "v1"):
        self._schemas = schemas
        self.urn_prefix = urn_prefix
        self.kinds = tuple(kinds)
        self.version = version
60→
    def for_kind(self, kind: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
        schema_id = f"{self.urn_prefix}{kind}:{self.version}"
        if kind not in self.kinds or schema_id not in self._schemas:
            raise SchemaProfileError(f"unknown schema kind: {kind!r}")
        return self._schemas[schema_id], schema_id

    def resolve(self, ref: str, base_id: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
        """Resolve ``#/$defs/x`` or ``<id>#/$defs/x``; return the node and the id of its owning schema."""
        document, _, fragment = ref.partition("#")
70→        owner = document or base_id

        if node is None:
            raise RefError(f"unknown schema {owner!r} in $ref {ref!r}")
        if fragment:

                raise RefError(f"unsupported $ref fragment in {ref!r}")
            node = node.get("$defs", {}).get(fragment[len("/$defs/"):])

80→        return node, owner

                  extra_dirs: tuple[Path, ...] = ()) -> Registry:
    """Load and profile-check schemas; cache by directory and registry parameters.

    ``version`` is the suffix of the ``$id`` of every kind (``<urn_prefix><kind>:<version>``). The schemas of

110→        try:

    """Load and profile-check one schema file whose ``$id`` must be ``<urn_prefix><kind>:<version>``.

    """Load one contract directory ``<contract>/v<N>/``; return its registry and its kind.

    The kind is the stem of the single ``<kind>.schema.json`` file and must equal the contract name; the
    ``$id`` must be ``<urn_prefix><kind>:v<N>`` for the version ``v<N>`` named by the directory.

150→    version, kind = directory.name, directory.parent.name
    if not _VERSION_DIR.fullmatch(version):
        raise SchemaProfileError(f"{directory}: directory name must be v<N>, got {version!r}")
    files = sorted(directory.glob("*.schema.json"))
    if [path.name for path in files] != [f"{kind}.schema.json"]:

    """Load a contract directory ``<contract>/v<N>/`` that holds several ``<kind>.schema.json`` documents.

    The kind of a document is the last segment of its ``$id``; every ``$id`` must be ``<prefix><kind>:v<N>`` for
    one ``<prefix>`` shared by the directory and for the version ``v<N>`` named by the directory. The file name is
    not read (it may spell the kind with dots). References to the foundation contracts resolve as in

170→    """

    version = directory.name
    if not _VERSION_DIR.fullmatch(version):
        raise SchemaProfileError(f"{directory}: directory name must be v<N>, got {version!r}")
    schemas = _read_schemas(directory)

    kinds: list[str] = []

180→        if match is None or match.group(3) != version:

200→

The `single` flag forces both base and current contracts to use the same loader. If the base is single but the current contract has a different URN prefix, the comparison may fail or miss changes. A concrete example of this mismatch is being worked out.

A new schema document is classified as `kind-added` and treated as informational. A breaking change inside a newly added document would therefore be reported as non-breaking. This is intentional design, not a bug.

A new hypothesis is being tested: if a new schema kind replaces inline content from an existing document, and the old document now `$ref`s that stricter kind, the comparison may miss the breaking change. Runtime `int | str` expressions are invalid on Python 3.9 because PEP 604 union syntax requires 3.10. Annotation-only usage is safe under `from __future__ import annotations`.

The `--base-root` test does exercise the override path. If the base root were ignored, the assertion for `property-added` would fail because the output would only contain `new` statuses.

A self-comparison test writes a schema to disk and then runs compatibility against itself. It expects no changes and a `compared` status.

A potential bug was found in kind extraction. For URIs containing the kind twice, such as `urn:swissknifeman:task:plan:plan:v1`, the extracted kind is `plan`. This could cause `compare` to target the wrong schema when resolving `$ref` pointers.

The comparison logic is being inspected for missed breaks. A schema change inside a document that is only a `$ref` target might be skipped if `compare` short-circuits identical root documents. # probe soundness in a throwaway git repo
HOME=$(mktemp -d)
export HOME

cd "$WORKDIR"
git init -q
git config user.email t@t
git config user.email t@t.dev
git config user.name t
mkdir -p packages/aicore/lib
# use the real library via PYTHONPATH later; this repo only holds schemas
python3 - << 'PY'
import json, os, shutil, subprocess, textwrap
from pathlib import Path
root = Path(".").resolve()
# minimal unit
def write(path, obj):
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(obj), encoding="utf-8")

def schema(dir, name, schema_id, body):
    doc = {"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "$id": schema_id, **body}
    write(dir / f"{name}.schema.json", doc)

base = root / "packages/mod/schemas"
# single-doc contract thing
schema(base/"thing"/"v1", "thing", "urn:swissknifeman:aicore:thing:v1",
       {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "properties": {"a": {"type": "string"}}})
# multi-doc plan with a def only reachable by $ref, and a kind that is only a $ref target
plan = base/"plan"/"v1"
prefix = "urn:swissknifeman:mod:plan:"
schema(plan, "defs", prefix+"defs:v1", {"$defs": {"id": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}}})
schema(plan, "item", prefix+"item:v1",
       {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
        "properties": {"id": {"$ref": prefix+"defs:v1#/$defs/id"}}})
# foundation schema referenced from outside the module root
found = root/"packages/aicore/schemas/artifact-ref/v1"
schema(found, "artifact-ref", "urn:swissknifeman:aicore:artifact-ref:v1",
       {"type": "string"})
ev = base/"event"/"v1"
schema(ev, "closed", "urn:swissknifeman:mod:event:closed:v1",
       {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False,
        "properties": {"ref": {"$ref": "urn:swissknifeman:aicore:artifact-ref:v1"}}})
unit = {"stability": "stable", "provides": {"contracts": [
    {"id": "urn:swissknifeman:mod:thing", "path": "schemas/thing/v1", "version": "v1", "stability": "stable"},
    {"id": "urn:swissknifeman:mod:plan", "path": "schemas/plan/v1", "version": "v1", "stability": "stable"},
    {"id": "urn:swissknifeman:mod:event", "path": "schemas/event/v1", "version": "v1", "stability": "stable"},
]}}
write(root/"packages/mod/unit.json", unit)
write(root/"packages/aicore/unit.json", {"stability": "stable", "provides": {"contracts": []}})
print("wrote", root)
PY
git add -A && git commit -q -m base
REPO="$WORKDIR"
LIB=/home/vostrikov/projects/packages/swissknifeman-next/packages/aicore/lib
run() {
  echo "----- $* -----"
  HOME=$(mktemp -d) PYTHONPATH="$LIB" python3 -m aicore schema compat --root "$REPO/packages/mod/schemas" "$@" ; echo EXIT:$?
}

import json
from pathlib import Path

  "$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",

  "type":"string"}))

content.thinking:
Continuing the review of P9.

P9.10 has a high-severity finding: schema compatibility checks resolve `$ref` against the current working-tree foundation schema rather than the base revision, so breaking changes in the foundation are invisible when comparing dependent contracts. A reproduction shows `schema compat --root packages/mod/schemas` exiting 0 after changing artifact-ref from string to integer.

The fallback is new code. Previously, unresolved foundation references caused a hard failure; now they silently resolve against the current working-tree schema, so breaking changes in the foundation between base and HEAD go unnoticed.

Internal `$ref`s in the same directory are correctly caught by comparison. The foundation schema is the only remaining gap.

The high severity is confirmed. A breaking change to the foundation schema alters the effective contract of every dependent document, yet compatibility checks report nothing. The break is only invisible to consumers; running compatibility on the foundation itself would catch it.

A second high-severity finding: `--base-root` set to the repository root or a typo path inside it causes every contract to be reported as new and compatibility to exit 0.

The reproduction confirms the bug: `--base-root .` and a typo path both report `plan/v1` as new and exit 0. This is a fail-open, so a breaking change would be missed.

The `--base-root` typo bug is rated high severity. A safety check that fails open on operator error is still a defect.

A potential issue with `_is_single` was noted: it compares schema filenames against a list of glob results, but glob order is arbitrary.

The `_is_single` concern is resolved. Glob order does not matter because the check only succeeds when exactly one schema file exists. Extra non-schema files are ignored. A single-to-multi transition was tested and correctly caught.

A new potential issue is being considered: an extra schema file in a directory could cause `load_contract_set` to refuse loading if the `$id` prefix does not match. This would abort the compatibility run with a hard error instead of reporting the breaking change, and other contracts might be skipped. The severity is uncertain, so a reproduction test is planned.

The `_is_single` concern is resolved. When a single-document base gains a second file, the original kind is still compared correctly. When a multi-document base becomes a single file with a different `$id` prefix, only the old kinds are marked removed and the new kind is marked added; the new file's content is not compared to any prior document.

The reverse single-to-multi transition is safe: if the new file's kind matches an old kind, that kind is compared and the rest are marked removed. The `_is_single` concern is resolved; with exactly one schema file, glob order does not matter.

The extra-file concern is resolved. If both base and current contain an extra schema file, it is treated as a new kind and compared normally. If only the current side has it, it is classified as a non-breaking addition. This behavior is intentional.

A new potential issue is being considered: if a schema filename contains an underscore, it may be excluded from the base snapshot by `_SCHEMA_FILE` while still present in the working tree. The kind would then appear only on the current side and be classified as added, hiding any tightening of the base schema.

The underscore filename concern is a latent soundness hole. The current schema filenames use dots and hyphens, so the regex does not exclude them. It remains untriggered unless an underscore file is introduced.

The `str | None` syntax is valid on Python 3.9. The bitwise `|` operator has always been legal, and PEP 604 only adds runtime evaluation.

A test hygiene issue was found in `test_the_repository_holds_plans`: it asserts that `plan_directories(ROOT / "plans")` is a list, but this check passes even when the returned list is empty.

The first test is weak because `assertIsInstance(..., list)` passes vacuously when the directory is empty. The second test only exercises code if plans actually exist. Severity is low.

The fixture README claims a byte-for-byte copy of an earlier version. The test only checks that the README text contains "never regenerate". The actual bytes match d3fd83e7, so the claim is accurate. This is not a finding.

The single-document contract test exercises the single-document path. It writes a thing schema and a plan contract unit.json, then runs compatibility; the schema is found on disk and compared correctly.

The single-document contract test is weak because it never asserts the shape of a change entry. With zero changes, a regression that adds `kind` to change objects would go undetected. Severity is low.

The first assertion in `test_the_base_may_live_under_another_root` only checks that the command exits with code 0. It does not verify that contracts are actually reported as new, so a silent failure would pass the test. The second half of the test does check the base-root path. This is weak test hygiene but not a standalone finding.

The human_view tolerance script must be run against the stable engine to confirm a count of 24. The `error_codes` logic could under-count or over-tolerate errors. The script might also miss plans outside `plans/` and `plans/archive/`. For P9.9, unchanged content is verified identical. Old paths in `ecosystem.md` and `source-index.json` still point to `workflow-craft` inside `skiller`; it is unclear whether that path belongs to `skiller` or the hub.

The skills test only checks name equality and manifest strings. It does not verify content unchanged, canonical paths, or that skiller omits the skill. The `skipIf` guard means the test is skipped when aicore is missing. The name assertion may be weak if `describe_skill` merely reads the directory name. Registry hashes for generated files still need verification against their sources. The public hygiene script also needs to be run.

I am checking whether removing the class_b projection is correct and whether bootstrap still generates a stale projection. The publication lock removed the entry, and the `.agents` skill was deleted, so I need to verify that no generated marketplace still lists it.

I will read doctor.py and publication.py changes next.

The skills test might not fail if workflow-craft lacks SKILL body checks, so I need to inspect describe_skill.

First-turn budget numbers show workflow-craft removed: ⊕48 and ↻3620.

The first-turn budget arithmetic checks out. The +5 character difference is in the axioma ecosystem-map body, not the always-resident prefix.

I will not run `skiller budget` to verify the first-turn numbers, because that CLI may write state and the instructions forbid running bin/* CLIs with state.

I will verify the skill hash against skills.json to confirm the registry entry is correct. I also need to inspect the golden generation.json diff and run the public-hygiene script. I should check whether any skiller tests still import the old workflow-craft path. The stale statement in ecosystem.md at line 425 claims workflow-craft remains in skiller; that file is the ecosystem map.

# Workflow-craft

A thin pointer skill to the canonical workflow-template constructor
20→(the Task package's `workflows/`). This is DISCIPLINE for activation and choice,
NOT a copy of template contents — template bodies and slot rules live in
the Task package's `workflows/README.md`; this skill points to them.

## When to activate

Use this skill when the user asks for:

- "write/compose/generate a workflow", "orchestrate subagents", "multi-agent
  run", "run several agents in parallel";
30→- authoring a `*.js` script for the Workflow tool (`scriptPath`/named-workflow);
- reworking/extending an already-existing plan workflow script.

**Field-case this skill closes:** a project is connected to skiller, the
constructor exists and its dev template already has optional review — and
the model still invents orchestration from scratch for a free-form phrasing
("compose a full-development workflow") and drops the optional review stage.
A free-form phrasing doesn't match any existing trigger — this skill's
`description` is the missing trigger.

40→**Boundary vs neighboring skills (don't blend):**

- `complex-task-orchestrator` — decomposing a task IN GENERAL (layers,
  invariants, DoD) inside ONE agent session, without spawning a separate
  `*.js` script and without launching subagents via the Workflow tool. If the
  output is an in-session action plan, not a workflow-script file — that's
  the other skill, not this one.
- `plan-protocol` — master-plan format and lifecycle (`plans/<ID>/`, phases,
  statuses, DoR/DoD). A master plan MAY spawn a workflow script for its
  execution phase (see "File location and name" below) — but the plan itself
50→  isn't about subagent orchestration, it's about framing the work.
- `/planner:make-workflow` (gate command, if present) — interview + generation +
  requested output reviewer around this same discipline. If the command is
  available, prefer it over manually following the skill: it guarantees a red
  reviewer verdict blocks the script from shipping unfixed.

## Procedure (in this order, don't reorder)

### 1. Match the 4 canonical templates first

60→Open the Task package's `workflows/README.md` — 4 parameterizable templates:
`wf-research-fanout.js`, `wf-author-by-spec.js`, `wf-audit-adversarial.js`,
`wf-dev-slice.js`. The constructor is a **library of portable templates, not
a code generator**: a task almost always fits one template or a pipeline of
several (research-fanout → author-by-spec/dev-slice → audit-adversarial).
Copy the matching template into the owning plan's `plans/<ID>/workflows/` and
fill the slots. If a task truly doesn't fit any template or their combination
— that's a deliberate exception (expensive-model main loop), not license to
silently write orchestration from scratch.

70→### 2. Mandatory stages by task type (SSOT matrix)

Workflows come in exactly two types, each with its own fixed set of mandatory
stages. Blending types or dropping a mandatory stage is a defect even if the
user didn't explicitly ask for it out loud (review for a dev workflow is
enabled only by explicit owner request).

| Type | Base templates | Mandatory stages | What's absent |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **Design** (design-only) | `wf-research-fanout.js`, `wf-audit-adversarial.js` | RAG research → design (expensive-model main loop) → self-check/DoR gate → optional requested read-only audit → one owning correction; re-audit only after changed evidence | code, tests, semver |
80→| **Development** (dev) | `wf-dev-slice.js`, `wf-author-by-spec.js` | slice → impl → tests-to-green → optional requested review → inter-slice gates → commit | design decisions on the cheap model (escalate to main loop, don't decide inline) |

This table is the skill's SSOT — the `/planner:make-workflow` command and its
output reviewer cite THIS table, not their own copy; fix drift here only.

Review and audit are opt-in: hard risks widen self-checks, not review admission. An explicit review
request can optionally select `--reviewer provider/model`; otherwise use the current native route.
Execution and review are separate calls, never recursive unbounded
fix/review. One owner `plan-run --reviewer` invocation may orchestrate both roles automatically,
retaining their independent sessions and bounded verdict history. The reviewer never repairs
90→product or starts its successor. Fill reviewer slots from the selected or current captured native route before
requested review; do not silently pick a default model. Repeated systemic class/area findings revise the
shared invariant model, and completed review rounds are bounded by Task's two-completed-round/one-correction policy. A
resume retains review history and unchanged evidence; it never resets a cap or broad-replays
previously accepted work. See the workflow README for slot details.

**Don't invent mandatory stages beyond this table** (source: the Task package's `workflows/README.md`) — if it seems
like another mandatory stage is needed, propose a matrix edit explicitly,
don't quietly bolt it onto one script.

100→**design ≠ dev, don't blend.** These are two disjoint requirement sets, not
two variants of one set: a design-only script with an `impl`/`tests` step, or
a dev script that omits explicitly requested review, are equally defective (the first
turns a design session into unplanned code on the cheap model, the second
reproduces the exact vaulter field-case). Determine the type BEFORE
generation (the template-matching step already hints the type:
research-fanout/audit-adversarial → design-only, dev-slice/author-by-spec →
dev) and run the whole script down one column of the table — don't mix in
stages from the other column "just in case".

110→### 2.1 Reference scripts (field prototypes of both types)

Real workflow scripts from other plans in vault Brain serve as a shape
reference (stage structure, what each type does NOT contain) — **cross-ref by
absolute path, don't vendor** (they belong to other plans; a copy drifts from
the source):

- **design-only, high-water-mark:** `~/Vaults/Brain/plans/
  EDUFY-2/workflows/wf-edufy-2-design-wave.js` — the strongest live example
  surveyed (findings P1-recon §1.4 "Reference irony"): `// SLOT:` markers on
120→  every constant (the only one of ~44 fleet files carrying them), judge-panel
  gated ONLY on the high-stakes phase (`JUDGE_PHASES`/`JUDGE_QUORUM`, not
  everywhere), `MAX_FIX_ROUNDS` on EVERY audit→fix cycle (not just the main
  one), pipeline + phase dependency graph. Look at its structure FIRST — it's
  above the baseline of the two references below.
- **design-only, baseline:** `~/Vaults/Brain/plans/ECOSYSTEM/
  workflows/wf-design-fleet.js` — RAG research → design → adversarial
  audit/DoR gate → fixes → re-audit, with zero lines of code/tests.
- **dev, baseline:** `~/Vaults/Brain/plans/AGENTOOLS/workflows/
  wf-agentools-drive.js` — slice → impl → tests-to-green → review → gates →
130→  commit, with a `designOnly` slot flag branching between the two modes
  within one template family; L195 is a guarded-optional-args example
  (`typeof args === 'string' ? JSON.parse(args) : (args || {})`).

If the file is unreachable (vault not mounted on the executing machine) —
don't fail and don't invent content: use the path as a cross-ref only and the
table above as the requirement source.

### 3. Slot rules — by reference, don't duplicate

140→How to fill slots (constants in the script header, `// SLOT:` markers
recommended but not mandatory; embedded config instead of an args string;
structured-summary-by-schema for **control-flow agents**, action/mechanical
agents may return prose; judge-panel only for high-stakes; max-iteration on
every loop-until; top-level `return report` is a sanctioned runtime idiom, not
a defect) — see the Task package's `workflows/README.md` §"Slot-filling rules".
Started retelling these rules here instead of linking — stop, that's a
constructor duplicate.

### 4. File location and name
150→
The script is an artifact of the owning plan: `plans/<ID>/workflows/wf-<plan-
id-lower>-<purpose>.js`, not a free location in the repo. If the task isn't
tied to a master plan (a one-off run outside `plans/`) that's an exception,
but the canon is mandatory whenever a plan exists (see `plan-protocol` — the
"two homes" scheme).

### 4.1 Anti-relaunch discipline (co-developing a workflow inside a session)

The run-report field `workflow_relaunch` (harness detector `_lib.py`, fires at
160→≥3 launches/resumes of one workflow in one session) is not a core-tool bug:
`resumeFromRunId` after an `Edit` to the script is a documented, sanctioned
pattern ("the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached
results instantly"). Field precedent (
): a dterema session called `Workflow` 15×
in a row — not "relaunch without a signal", but **8 rounds of fixing the
workflow script from inside the main interactive session** (relative-path
bug, top-level `return`, gate prompt missing scope, docblock/formatting,
review-prompt text fixed twice), each fix → commit → `resumeFromRunId`. The
signal is a diagnostic proxy — "script was written and fanned out untested" —
170→not an alarm.

**Rule:** before calling `Workflow` on a script you just wrote or heavily
edited, dry-run its syntax/logic on a minimal data slice (or at least
`node --check`) in an isolated dev-loop, rather than treating the fan-out
itself as your linter. If `workflow_relaunch` still fires (many resumes on
one script this session) — that's not cause for alarm (the process is
sanctioned), but it IS cause to fix one bug per resume deliberately rather
than silently piling up iterations: note in the script comment what each fix
addressed, so `analyst digest` (candidate lesson `workflow-relaunch`) and the
180→next session see the fix history, not just the final version.

**Checkpoint before a third resume in a row: is my cache-bust marker
global?** A second field precedent on the same project/script (`dterema`,
`wf-dterema-site-p3-api.js`, 2026-07-15) burned ≈4M subagent tokens in one
day: the script held ONE global `GATE_ASOF` constant pasted into the code-gate,
bookkeeping-gate and review prompts of EVERY pipeline item. Each bump — made to
re-verify a SINGLE item being fixed — invalidated the `agent()` cache for
already-closed items too, so the resume re-ran gate+review over files that
hadn't changed by a line. Rule: a manual invalidator is a **per-item field
190→only** (`s.asOf`, mixed into that item's prompt/`label` — see README "slot
rules" → per-item cache-bust), never a global constant across all prompts.
Better still, no manual marker: the gate prompt already asks the agent to check
`git log`/HEAD, so freshness is verified live; forcing is needed only after an
external fix commit and must stay local.

### 5. RAG option for non-standard orchestration

If the task needs orchestration the 4 templates don't cover directly (rare,
not the first choice) — before inventing a pattern from scratch, check
200→current practice via `research/query-craft` (how to phrase the query) →
`general/verify-claims` (when/how to verify). Mark the result in the script
comment: `RAG:✅ <date> <source>` or `[UNVERIFIED]` if the engine was
unavailable — don't pass off unverified orchestration as verified.

## Checklist before shipping a script

- [ ] Task checked against the 4 templates first — not written from scratch
      if it fits.
- [ ] Type determined (design-only / dev), matrix's mandatory stages present.
210→- [ ] Slot rules followed (constants, embedded config, structured-summary,
      max-iteration) — per README, not from memory.
- [ ] File location and name — canon `plans/<ID>/workflows/wf-<id>-
      <purpose>.js`.
- [ ] Non-standard orchestration marked RAG:✅/[UNVERIFIED].

## Related skills

- `general/complex-task-orchestrator` — decomposing a task within one session
  without spawning a separate workflow script (boundary above).
220→- `general/plan-protocol` — master-plan format; the workflow script is an
  artifact of the plan's execution phase, "two homes" sets its canonical
  location.
- `general/spec-interview` — the "one question at a time" mechanic used by
  the `/planner:make-workflow` gate command when clarifying template slots.
- `research/query-craft` — how to phrase a RAG query for non-standard
  orchestration (step 5).
- `general/verify-claims` — when and how to verify an external fact at all.
